newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn plans supplementary 1997 budget - Bohl.
newsitem.headline: Bonn plans supplementary 1997 budget - Bohl.

text.p: The German government said on Friday it would draft a supplementary 1997 budget which will allow a higher level of new borrowing than planned but still meet the criteria for Europe's single currency.
Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said in a statement that the supplementary budget would "make an exceptional allowance for higher new borrowing".

Commenting on the 1998 budget, which is currently being drafted by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's three-party coalition, Bohl said it would meet constitutional requirements that new borrowing does not exceed investment.

"With that we will fulfil the Maastricht criteria to participate in European monetary union. Through budget measures already introduced, among others privatisation, Germany will definitely meet the three percent criterion," Bohl said.

It was not immediately clear if Bohl's comment on higher new borrowing this year meant Bonn was distancing itself from its drive to cut the deficit to exactly three percent of GDP, rather than use the room for manoeuvre contained in the wording of the Maastricht treaty.

The remarks on fulfilling the Maastricht deficit target were also ambiguous, and it was not clear whether they applied to both 1997 and 1998, or just to 1998. No officials at the Chancellery or Finance Ministries were available for comment.
